title: What Happens If You Hold in a Sneeze?
sources: BMJ Case Reports, Spontaneous tracheal rupture from sneezing
Harvard Health Publishing, Sneezing pressure dynamics

lines.text: What actually happens if you pinch your nose and hold in a sneeze?
lines.caps: What happens if | you hold in | a *sneeze?

lines.text: A normal sneeze blasts air out of your lungs at over one hundred miles per hour.
lines.caps: Blasts air out | at *100 miles | per *hour

lines.text: When you clamp your mouth and nose shut, that massive pressure has nowhere to escape.
lines.caps: Closing your nose | traps *massive pressure | inside

lines.text: The explosive force gets redirected backwards up your Eustachian tubes.
This can violently rupture your delicate eardrum, causing permanent hearing damage.
In extreme cases, the pressure can tear your pharynx or push air into your chest cavity.
lines.caps: Can tear your *throat | and push air | into your *chest

lines.text: So whenever you feel a sneeze coming, never hold it in. Just let it fly!
lines.caps: Never *hold it in | just let it *fly!
